[countering Rotschreck]

> Because it is very hard to deal with it, well let me correct myself it
> is impossible to counter it effectively.

Methods to deal with Rotschreck:
a) Use Psyche to restart combat. Thanks to the May rulings.
b) Use Telepathic Tracking to start another round. Ditto.
c) Don't get blocked.
d) Realize that your predator or prey can only play *one* per turn, and they're
losing MPAs that they could be using for pool gain or something exciting like
that, suck it up, and simply rescue the vampire that went down.
e) As a last resort, you could stop taking actions.

Xian

[errata for Rotschreck?]

> Because it is very hard to deal with it, well let me correct myself it
> is impossible to counter it effectively.

I dunno, I've never seen a really "dominating" Rotschreck deck.
Yes, it can be very difficult to avoid getting a vampire sent
to torpor once per turn. But that shouldn't be enough to keep
you from ousting them. If you're playing combat, you can beat
up all their vampires with impunity after they've used their
one Rotschreck. If you're playing vote, you can call votes and
not worry about getting Rotschrecked after the first one. If
you're playing bleed, likewise.

If they're playing so much intercept/blocking that you won't be
able to get *any* actions through (as their predator) and so
will be unable to rescue your Rotschrecked vampires *or* do any
damage to them, then they're playing a deck that automatically
loses, as far as I can tell. You can't win games by ousting
your predator. You just give the game away to someone else
(your grandpredator for example). If that's what they're doing,
they should stop playing to lose. :-)

Josh

Messages.Author: Halcyan 2

>Argh. Don't talk to be about table splitting. :-P

>In my opinion - and in tournaments I run - it's almost never
>legal to make a deal specifically to help someone else win a
>game.

Actually, when I referred to splitting and divvying up points I was thinking
more along the lines of a classic 2-1-1-1-0 type of split (as opposed to
deal-making). Splitting up the VP's among many players.

I've found it common when everyone brings power bleed decks. Say a 5-player
game A-->B-->C-->D-->E and you're A. Now C is close to ousting D and D is close
to ousting E. If you do nothing, C takes out D and finishes up the much
weakened E, gaining 2 VP's and lots of pool. But say you can oust E, giving D a
single VP and 6 pool. The 6 pool will provide a bit more of a speedbump (but
not enough to prevent his inevitable ousting) and by splitting up the VP's
among the players, you have a better chance at a Table Win.

Of course it really helps if you can bleed other players (Raphael, Julia, Night
Moves, Cat Burglary, Kindred Spirits, etc.) or you can do vote damage to them.

If you know that your deck can take out your prey in a long protracted game but
you're worried about the other players, it can sometimes be to your benefit to
have each player taken out in turn. (Though it gets messy when someone dies out
of turn. I suppose that's what Life Boon's for).

Halcyan 2
